===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|stŭd'''′'''ē}}

** {{audio|en|En-uk-to study.ogg|a=UK}}

* {{IPA|en|/(ɪ)ˈsʈəɖ.i/|a=Indic}}
* {{rhymes|en|ʌdi|s=2}}
* {{hyph|en|study}}

===Etymology 1===
{{etymon|en|id=verb|:inh|enm:studien}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*(s)tewd-}}
{{inh+|en|enm|studien}}, from {{der|en|fro|estudier}} (Modern {{m+|fr|étudier}}), from {{m|fro|estudie|pos=n}}, {{lg|loanword|borrowed}} from {{der|en|la|studium}}. {{displaced|ang|cneordlæcan}}.

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|usually|academic|transitive|intransitive}} To [[review]] materials already learned in order to make sure one does not forget them, usually in preparation for an [[examination]].
#: {{uxa|en|Students are expected to start '''studying''' for final exams in March.}}
#: {{uxa|en|I need to '''study''' my biology notes.}}
# {{lb|en|academic|transitive}} To take a [[course]] or courses on a subject.
#: {{uxa|en|I '''study''' medicine at the university.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[acquire]] [[knowledge]] on a [[subject]] with the [[intention]] of [[apply]]ing it in [[practice]].
#: {{uxa|en|Biologists '''study''' living things.}}
#: {{uxa|en|In 2015, scientists found that 82 percent of glaciers '''studied''' in China had decreased in size.|footer=[[File:In 2015, scientists found that.ogg]]}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To look at [[carefully]] and [[minutely]].
#: {{uxa|en|He '''studied''' the map in preparation for the hike.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To fix the mind closely upon a subject; to dwell upon anything in thought; to muse; to ponder.
#* '''July 10, 1732''', {{w|Jonathan Swift}}, [[s:The Works of the Rev. Jonathan Swift/Volume 12/From Jonathan Swift to John Gay and Catherine Hyde - 6|letter]] to Mr. Gay and The Duchess of Queensberry
# {{lb|en|archaic|intransitive}} To [[endeavor]] diligently; to be [[zealous]].
#* {{RQ:KJV|1 Thessalonians|4|11|passage=And that ye '''study''' to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands, as we commanded you {{...}}}}

===Etymology 2===
{{inh+|en|enm|studie}}, from {{der|en|fro|estudie}} (Modern {{m+|fr|étude}}), {{lg|loanword|borrowed}} from {{der|en|la|studium||[[zeal]], [[dedication]], study}},{{ref|name=voed|{{cite-book|en|title=Oxford English Dictionary|edition=1st|entry=study, ''v.''|publisher=Oxford University Press|location=Oxford|year=1919}}}}{{ref|name=noed|{{cite-book|en|title=Oxford English Dictionary|edition=1st|entry=study, ''n.''|publisher=Oxford University Press|location=Oxford|year=1919}}}} from {{der|en|ine-pro|*(s)tewd-||to push, to hit}}. {{doublet|en|etude|studio}}.

====Noun====
{{en-noun|~}}

# Mental effort to acquire [[knowledge]] or learning.
#: {{uxa|en|The '''study''' of languages is fascinating.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1661|author1={{w|John Fell (bishop)|Fell, John}}|title=The Life of the most learned, reverend and pious Dr. H. Hammond|url=https://archive.org/details/a615775104worduoft|page=334|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/a615775104worduoft/page/334/mode/1up|passage=During the whole time of his abode in the university he generally spent thirteen hours of the day in '''study'''; by which assiduity besides an exact dispatch of the whole course of philosophy, he read over in a manner all classic authors that are extant;{{nb...}}.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1699|author1={{w|Sir William Temple, 1st Baronet|Temple, William}}|title=Heads designed for an essay on conversations|url=https://essays.quotidiana.org/temple/heads_for_conversation/|passage='''Study''' gives strength to the mind; conversation, grace: the first apt to give stiffness, the other suppleness: one gives substance and form to the statue, the other polishes it.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2012|month=March-April|author=John T. Jost
|volume=100|issue=2|page=162|magazine=w:American Scientist
|title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/bookshelf/pub/social-justice-is-it-in-our-nature-and-our-future Social Justice: Is It in Our Nature (and Our Future)?]
|passage=He draws eclectically on '''studies''' of baboons, descriptive anthropological accounts of hunter-gatherer societies and, in a few cases, the fossil record.}}
# The act of studying or examining; [[examination]].
#: {{uxa|en|I made a careful '''study''' of his sister.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2013|month=September-October|author=[http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/katie-l-burke Katie L. Burke]
|magazine=w:American Scientist|title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/pub/2013/5/in-the-news-47 In the News]
|passage=Oxygen levels on Earth skyrocketed 2.4 billion years ago, when cyanobacteria evolved photosynthesis:{{...}}. The evolutionary precursor of photosynthesis is still under debate, and a new '''study''' sheds light. The critical component of the photosynthetic system is the “water-oxidizing complex”, made up of manganese atoms and a calcium atom.}}
# Any particular branch of learning that is studied; any object of attentive consideration.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1762|author1={{w|Edmund Law|Law, Edmund}}|title=An extract from: A serious call to a devout and holy life|passage=The Holy Scriptures, especially the New Testament, are her daily '''study'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Pope Essay on Man|II|passage=The proper '''study''' of mankind is man.}}
# {{senseid|en|room}} A [[room]] in a house intended for reading and writing; traditionally the private room of the male head of household.
#: {{syn|en|home office|cabinet|closet<l:archaic>}}
#: {{cot|en|boudoir<qq:female equivalent>}}
#: {{uxa|en|Father spends all his time in the '''study''' poring over manuscripts.}}
#* {{RQ:Hawthorne Scarlet Letter|Introductory|passage=his cheery little '''study'''}}
#* {{quote-web|en|date=2025-08-14|url=https://www.msn.com/en-ca/money/personalfinance/i-m-sick-of-my-rich-friends-pretending-that-they-re-struggling/ar-AA1KuvVk|work={{w|The i Paper}}|author=Anniki Sommerville|title=I’m sick of my rich friends pretending that they’re struggling|passage=I was asked round once for dinner, and my tongue was hanging out at the sheer scale of it – complete with three bathrooms, two '''studies''', and a sauna.}}
# An [[artwork]] made in order to [[practise]] or [[demonstrate]] a subject or technique.
#: {{coa|en|a '''study''' of heads or of hands for a figure picture}}
# The human face, bearing an expression which the observer finds amusingly typical of a particular emotion or state of mind.
#: {{uxa|en|Geoffrey's face was a '''study'''.}}
#: {{uxa|en|Geoffrey's face was a '''study''' in amazement {{q-q|or in bewilderment, irritation, distress etc.}}}}
# {{lb|en|music}} A piece for special practice; an [[etude]].
# {{lb|en|academic}} An [[academic]] [[publication]].
#: {{uxa|en|That new '''study''' on noncommutative symmetries looks promising.}}
# {{senseid|en|actor}} One who commits a [[theatrical]] [[part]] to [[memory]].
# {{lb|en|chess}} An [[endgame]] problem composed for artistic merit, where one side is to play for a win or for a draw.
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} A state of mental [[perplexity]] or worried thought.
#* {{RQ:Mlry MrtDrthr|3.18|2|I|xx|passage=wel said the kynge thow mayst take myn hors by force but and I myȝte preue the whether thow were better on horsbak or I / wel said the knyght seke me here whan thow wolt and here nygh this wel thow shalt fynde me / and soo passyd on his weye / thenne the kyng sat in a '''study''' and bad his men fetche his hors as faste as euer they myghte
|translation=Well, said the king, thou mayst take my horse by force, but an I might prove thee whether thou were better on horseback or I. Well, said the knight, seek me here when thou wilt, and here nigh this well thou shalt find me, and so passed on his way. Then the king sat in a study, and bade his men fetch his horse as fast as ever they might.}}
#* {{RQ:Eddison Worm|page=36|passage=When they had stood for a while without speech, gazing over the sea, Gro spake and said, “Consider how as day now dieth in yonder chambers of the west, so hath the glory departed from Witchland.” ¶ But the Red Foliot answered him not, being in a '''study'''.}}
# {{lb|en|archaic}} [[thought|Thought]], as directed to a specific purpose; one's [[concern]].
#: {{uxa|en|My '''study''' was to avoid disturbing her.}}
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=10|passage=Just men they seemd, and all thir '''study''' bent / To worship God aright, and know his works.|year=1873}}
